sections.h2: How quickly can a Midland house change hands?
sections.html:
Quickly, when the price reflects condition. Midland has an energy-driven economy, and investors, landlords and cash buyers all buy there. The usual trade applies: speed and certainty against top price.

Ask every buyer how long a written offer stays open, and compare the offers side by side.

Midland calls itself the heart of the Permian Basin, and energy companies and Midland ISD are among its largest employers. The metro population is reported at 193,139 for 2026, up 8.1 percent from 2020, with a median age of 31.5.

A younger population tends to include renters and first-time buyers, so an investor or a buyer using financing may both compete for your house. Apartment rents are rising while occupancy has improved, which is relevant if your buyer is an investor. Rely on written offers and an agent's comparable sales for pricing, since citywide figures say little about one house.

sections.h2: Which selling routes make sense in Midland?
sections.html:
The usual choices are a listing, a direct cash sale or a local investor. Let the condition of the house guide you, not the biggest number.

  • Agent listing. Fits move-in-ready houses; you carry repairs and financing risk.
  • Cash buyer. Handles foundation, roof, plumbing or wiring problems and short-notice relocations.
  • Investor with a short close or leaseback. Gives you time to move out.
  • Keep and rent. Practical only if you can manage repairs and turnover from afar.

Work out what you would actually keep after fees, repairs and carrying costs under each.

sections.h2: Midland permits that could trip up a sale
sections.html:
A residential permit is needed in Midland for new construction, additions, remodels, repairs and detached accessory buildings, and it is pulled by the owner or by a bonded contractor on the city's registry.

Work must begin within 180 days of issue, and a permit lapses if building halts for more than 180 days. You email the request to the permit clerk, paying 25 percent of the fee when you submit and 75 percent on approval. Plan on 5 to 7 business days for review. If earlier work went unpermitted, ask the city how to document it before an inspector raises it.

Anyone running a short-term rental also owes a seven percent hotel occupancy tax to the city on the price paid.

Midland homeowners get school-district homestead relief plus local options. The Midland Central Appraisal District lists the amounts for each taxing unit, which matters to a buyer reading your tax history.

Midland Central Appraisal District homestead and senior exemptions

Disabled-veteran exemptions run from $5,000 up to $12,000 off assessed value by rating, with 100 percent homesteadable value for a full rating.

Tenants and trespassers are handled differently. A tenant must be eviction-processed: a written notice of at least three days, unless the lease differs, and then a justice court case that has its hearing 10 to 21 days after filing. Someone who moved in without permission may be removable faster.

Property Code chapter 24B covers a non-family occupant who was never a tenant. The owner can ask the sheriff or constable to remove that person without a court case, provided the occupant stayed after being told to go and no suit is pending. Removing the wrong person invites a lawsuit, so check each condition with the sheriff's office first.

  • After a judgment, a writ of possession must issue within 60 days, though a court can stretch that to 90 for good cause.
  • Many cash buyers will purchase an occupied home, so you do not have to wait.

Having these ready saves time with the title company.

  • Deed and mortgage payoff statement.
  • Latest tax bill, plus any exemption notice the appraisal district sent.
  • Permit records for remodels, repairs or outbuildings.
  • Lease and rent roll if someone lives there.
  • Roof, water or foundation reports.

Midland takes permit requests by email, so keep scans of old permits handy. If a permit is missing, call the permit clerk at 432-685-7390.

After the contract is signed, a title company handles the paperwork. It combs county records for liens, back taxes and anything clouding ownership, and asks you for a payoff letter and tax bill. A problem it finds, say a contractor's lien from old work or a co-owner who never signed, must be fixed before the deed can change hands.

At closing you sign the deed and the county clerk records it. The title company then pays off your loan and your share of taxes and sends you the balance. A buyer using a mortgage brings an appraisal and underwriting, and either can renegotiate the price. Cash buyers usually skip both, so their sales can wrap up sooner.

sections.h2: Selling a house that needs work
sections.html:
Shifting foundations, tired roofs and bad plumbing or wiring tend to turn away financed buyers, since lenders and appraisers insist on repairs first. A cash buyer builds the repair into the offer and takes the house as is. You avoid contractor bids, permits and months of carrying costs.

Get any offer in writing with the price, closing date and closing cost split spelled out, then compare it with what a fixed-up listing would net after fees. When the numbers land close together, the quicker sale usually makes more sense.

Midland's strategic plan includes capital projects, parks, downtown redevelopment and economic zones. Street, drainage or downtown work near your address can change how buyers see the block, so ask the city's planning office what is scheduled near you.

sections.h2: When Texas tax bills come due
sections.html:
Statements go out near October 1, and a bill still unpaid after January 31 is delinquent. February 1 brings a six percent penalty and one percent interest, with further charges each month after that.

The lien for the year belongs to whoever owned the house on January 1. Typically the title company splits the bill between buyer and seller and takes your part from the proceeds. To protest your value, file by mid-May or within 30 days of your notice, whichever comes later.

The person who signs the deed has to show they have the authority. Depending on the case, that means an administrator's deed, a muniment of title order, a recorded affidavit of death paired with a transfer on death deed, or as a last resort an affidavit of heirship.

A small-estate affidavit works when everything apart from the homestead adds up to $75,000 or less and every heir agrees.

sections.h2: Questions to ask a cash buyer
sections.html: Find out who the buyer is, whether the price covers the whole house as is, and who holds earnest money. Ask how many days to close and what happens if a lien surfaces. Read the contract before committing, and let the title company prepare the closing statement.

faqs.q: Is selling as-is allowed in Midland?
faqs.a: Cash buyers regularly purchase houses with foundation, roof or plumbing problems. The offer will reflect the repair cost.
Repairs, remodels, additions and detached accessory buildings. An owner or registered bonded contractor applies, and a permit lapses if work does not begin within 180 days.

faqs.q: What homestead relief does a Midland buyer get?
faqs.a: Midland ISD gives $140,000 plus a 10 percent local option. A purchaser may claim it right away if you never did.

faqs.q: Who settles the tax bill when the sale closes?
faqs.a: The title company, normally, with your share taken from proceeds. The lien attaches January 1, so read the split on the closing statement.

faqs.q: What paperwork proves I can sell an inherited house?
faqs.a: Court or recorded documents showing authority: a muniment of title, administration, a transfer on death deed, or an affidavit of heirship.
